Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out as a critical darling, earning an 85/100 score for its unexpectedly moving story about robot companionship. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** has become the season's breakout comedy hit, with Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln delighting critics and audiences alike with its irreverent humor.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves through spring 2026, the play landscape offers an eclectic mix ranging from intimate comedic farces to spectacular technical showcases. This month's selections average a solid 77 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a season where theatrical ambition runs high even when execution varies.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln that continues to draw raves for its audacious premise and sharp comedic execution. Critics consistently highlight the show's willingness to push boundaries, transforming a historical figure into a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist with surprisingly effective results. With an 84/100 rating across 33 reviews, it represents the kind of original, risk-taking work that keeps Broadway vital.

**Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** maintains its position as a technical marvel, earning an 82/100 from 69 critics who remain impressed by its stagecraft and magical illusions even as opinions diverge on the narrative's effectiveness. The production demonstrates how spectacle and theatrical innovation can sustain a show despite story concerns.

Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** illustrates the challenge of translating screen properties to stage. While critics acknowledge its impressive special effects and technical ambition, the three-hour prequel struggles with narrative bloat, earning a more modest 66/100 across 35 reviews.

This month's offerings underscore Broadway's current identity: a landscape where innovative comedies, established magical spectacles, and ambitious adaptations compete for attention. Whether you're drawn to irreverent humor, theatrical wizardry, or franchise world-building, consult the detailed reviews below to find your next theater experience.

best-broadway-shows-for-kids.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows for Kids

Broadway in March 2026 offers a robust selection of family-friendly productions, from long-running spectacles to magical adventures that continue to captivate young audiences. With six shows currently recommended for families, the options span Disney classics, literary adaptations, and biographical musicals that appeal to multiple generations.

**The Lion King** remains the gold standard for theatrical family entertainment, earning the highest critical marks at 83/100. Now in its third decade on Broadway, Julie Taymor's visionary production continues to astonish with its innovative puppetry and transformative stagecraft that turns the Minskoff Theatre into the African savanna. Close behind is **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child**, which scores 82/100 on the strength of its spectacular magical illusions and technical wizardry, though critics note the narrative doesn't quite match the stagecraft's ambition.

The remaining selections—**Aladdin**, **& Juliet**, **Wicked**, and **MJ The Musical**—all cluster around the 70-71/100 range, each offering distinct appeals. Aladdin delivers classic Disney spectacle, while & Juliet provides a contemporary pop-music twist on Shakespeare. Wicked continues its reign as a Broadway institution with powerhouse vocals, and MJ The Musical showcases electrifying dance performances that bring Michael Jackson's artistry to the stage.

The average critical score of 75/100 across these six productions reflects a healthy ecosystem of family entertainment, though parents should note that age-appropriateness varies significantly between shows. Consider your children's ages, attention spans, and interests when selecting from this month's offerings.

In sharp contrast, **Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)** arrives from London as a modest two-hander that charms critics with its simplicity. This British rom-com eschews spectacle for sincerity, and reviewers respond warmly to its heartfelt performances and unpretentious approach to storytelling. At 77 from 26 reviews, it proves that intimate theatrical experiences continue to find their audience alongside Broadway's larger productions.

Meanwhile, **Chess** generates the most divided critical response of the month. The ABBA-penned score and vocal performances from Lea Michele, Aaron Tveit, and their co-star earn consistent praise, but critics remain split on the production's overall execution, resulting in a 65 average across 29 reviews.

With an overall average score of 75 across these three productions, March presents theatergoers with options that span Broadway's full range—from socially conscious period drama to contemporary romantic comedy to classic musical spectacle. Whether you're drawn to critical favorites or curious about more polarizing productions, this month's slate offers entry points for various theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway shows that opened in 2020—a year that would soon see theaters go dark for an unprecedented period—five productions stand out for their artistic ambition and critical reception.

Leading the pack is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its grittier approach to the beloved musical, though the production's darker tone doesn't win over everyone. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** makes its long-overdue Broadway debut with a 78/100 score across 29 reviews. Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama about racial tension in a World War II Army base proves remarkably resonant in this acclaimed revival, demonstrating the enduring power of its examination of prejudice and identity.

The remaining shows reflect Broadway's range in early 2020. Laura Linney anchors **My Name is Lucy Barton**, a solo adaptation that divides critics despite universal praise for her performance. **Grand Horizons** offers more traditional fare—a boulevard comedy about late-life divorce that critics find pleasant if familiar, buoyed by performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Rounding out the selection, Ivo van Hove's **West Side Story** takes the biggest creative risks, with its radical reimagining earning both passionate admirers and skeptical detractors.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of early 2020 represents a snapshot of Broadway at a pivotal moment—just before everything changed. For theatergoers interested in this era, these shows offer a compelling mix of bold reinventions and powerful dramatic revivals worth exploring.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

Nearly five years after Broadway's historic reopening following the COVID-19 shutdown, the shows that debuted in 2021 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and artistic ambition. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 81/100 critic score—represents one of the most diverse and experimental periods in recent Broadway history, mixing bold reinventions of classics with groundbreaking new work.

The standout remains **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to recorded interviews with Hnath's mother. Critics consistently describe the production as unforgettable and unlike anything else on Broadway. **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** proves equally transformative, with Rebecca Frecknall's immersive staging completely reimagining the August Wilson Theatre's interior to create an enveloping nightclub environment that critics call essential theater. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy**, Sam Mendes's epic three-and-a-half-hour examination of American capitalism, earns widespread praise as a theatrical triumph combining extraordinary performances with stunning visual direction.

The 2021 season also marks significant milestones: **Pass Over** opened as Broadway's first production following the shutdown, while **The Phantom of the Opera** began its final run after decades as Broadway's longest-running show. Experimental works like **Is This a Room**—built entirely from FBI transcripts—share space with crowd-pleasing revivals like **SIX** and **Company**, demonstrating Broadway's range from intimate drama to spectacular musical entertainment.

Whether you're drawn to innovative theatrical experiments or reimagined classics, these productions from 2021's landmark season offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway at its most daring and diverse.

The wide variance in reception—from enthusiastic praise to lukewarm responses—underscores how even well-known properties require fresh creative vision to resonate with contemporary audiences.

As more productions open and accumulate reviews throughout the spring, theatergoers should monitor how these shows develop and which productions gain momentum with both critics and audiences.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theatrical ambition cut short by unprecedented circumstances. While the pandemic would soon shutter theaters for over a year, these productions—many enjoying extended runs or revivals—continue to shape conversations about what contemporary theater can achieve.

**A Soldier's Play** stands as the highest-rated production among currently running shows from that year, earning an impressive 78/100 from critics. Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally received its long-overdue Broadway premiere in a revival that critics consistently describe as powerful and urgent, proving the play's examination of race and identity within the military remains devastatingly relevant.

The year also brought bold reimaginings of classics. A grittier reboot of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre earns an 83/100, with critics praising its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though purists remain divided. Meanwhile, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** proves the most polarizing entry, with some critics celebrating its visceral, video-enhanced staging while others question whether the experimental approach serves Bernstein and Sondheim's material.

More intimate offerings round out the selection, including Laura Linney's solo turn in **My Name is Lucy Barton** and the pleasant if familiar boulevard comedy **Grand Horizons**, both elevated by luminous star performances.

With an average critical score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates both the enduring power of classical material and theater's ongoing struggle to balance innovation with tradition. Explore our detailed reviews to find which of these productions deserves your attention.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—a season defined by the industry's triumphant return following the pandemic shutdown and marked by bold artistic experimentation.

The ten productions featured here average an impressive 81/100 from critics, reflecting a year when artists pushed boundaries and reimagined what Broadway could be. Leading the field is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance, earning it the highest critical score at 86/100. Close behind, **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** transforms the August Wilson Theatre into an immersive Weimar-era nightclub, with Rebecca Frecknall's acclaimed revival scoring 83/100.

The season showcased remarkable diversity in theatrical storytelling. Verbatim dramas like **Is This a Room** transformed FBI transcripts into pulse-pounding theater, while solo performances such as **Lackawanna Blues** demonstrated the power of one actor embodying entire worlds. Epic narratives like **The Lehman Trilogy** traced 163 years of American capitalism, and contemporary works including **Pass Over** and **Clyde's** brought urgent social commentary to Broadway stages.

Musical theater also flourished, from **Company**'s gender-swapped Sondheim revival to **SIX**'s pop-concert reimagining of Tudor history, alongside **The Phantom of the Opera**'s continuing reign as Broadway's longest-running show at the time.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection represents a pivotal moment when Broadway returned with renewed creative ambition.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2022 stands out as a remarkable period of artistic achievement, marked by an exceptional concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and critically acclaimed revivals that continue to resonate with audiences today.

The ten productions featured in this guide maintain an impressive average critic score of 83/100, reflecting a season of consistently high-quality theater. Leading the field is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical that critics hailed as a near-perfect achievement, masterfully balancing laugh-out-loud comedy with profound emotional depth. Close behind, **Into the Woods** delivered a stripped-down Sondheim revival that served as both a fitting tribute to the late composer and a fresh interpretation that stood firmly on its own merits. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's groundbreaking meta-musical, rounded out the top tier with its brazenly original exploration of identity and creativity.

What distinguishes this collection is its remarkable diversity—from the electrifying performances in Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** revival to Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, from Mike Birbiglia's intimate one-man show to Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'**. Notably, four of the featured productions are Pulitzer Prize winners, underscoring the exceptional literary and theatrical merit of this season's offerings.

These productions represent more than just critical success; they capture a pivotal moment in Broadway's recovery and reinvention following the pandemic shutdown. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting familiar favorites, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the theatrical excellence that defined 2022's Broadway landscape.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the exceptional class of plays that opened on Broadway in 2023 continues to resonate with audiences and critics alike, representing one of the strongest theatrical years in recent memory. With an impressive average critic score of 82/100, these productions demonstrate the vitality and range of contemporary American theatre.

Leading the pack is Maria Friedman's triumphant revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has successfully redeemed Stephen Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop through emotionally resonant performances and fresh directorial vision. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that theatrical adaptations of popular franchises can transcend mere fan service, earning acclaim for its breathtaking technical achievements and compelling storytelling that stands independently of its source material.

The year also showcased powerful ensemble work in **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama led by Sarah Paulson, while **Purlie Victorious: A Non-Confederate Romp Through the Cotton Patch** brought long-overdue attention to Ossie Davis's 1961 satire, demonstrating its continued relevance six decades later. Meanwhile, the revival of **Parade** struck a chord with its urgent contemporary resonance, and the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham** offered a fresh, raucous take on Hamlet set at a Black family barbecue.

From solo performances like **Just for Us** to immersive experiences like **Stereophonic**, the 2023 season delivered remarkable variety alongside consistent quality. Whether you're drawn to classic revivals reimagined for modern audiences or bold new voices pushing theatrical boundaries, these ten productions represent essential viewing for anyone seeking to understand Broadway's current artistic landscape.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As we look back from March 2026, the 2024 Broadway season stands out as a remarkably diverse and critically acclaimed period for theatrical storytelling. The shows that debuted that year continue to resonate with audiences, earning an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across our featured productions.

Leading the pack is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's sprawling rock drama set in a 1970s recording studio, which critics consistently describe as a theatrical marvel. Its authentic depiction of the creative process and the tensions within a Fleetwood Mac-inspired band has earned it the highest marks of the season. Close behind is **Operation Mincemeat**, a grassroots British sensation that successfully made the leap from fringe theater to the West End, captivating critics with its inventive energy and ensemble work.

The 2024 season demonstrates Broadway's appetite for both intimate character studies and bold experimentation. **Cole Escola's Oh, Mary!** reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist in what critics call a comedic tour de force, while **Maybe Happy Ending** brings an unexpectedly moving robot love story to the musical theater canon. Traditional revivals also found their place, with Audra McDonald's interpretation of Mama Rose in **Gypsy** and a lavish new production of **Oliver!** earning strong reviews.

From Rachel Bloom's **Mary Jane**—an understated portrait of maternal devotion—to Justin Peck's dance-driven **Illinoise** and Shaina Taub's educational **Suffs**, the season offered something for every theatrical taste. Whether you're catching up on shows still running or exploring what made 2024 special, these productions represent some of the finest work Broadway had to offer.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2025

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the plays that debuted last year continue to demonstrate remarkable range and vitality. From intimate family dramas to spectacular musical adaptations, the 2025 season has proven to be one of substance and artistic ambition, with ten productions earning critical scores averaging 84/100.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down revival of **All My Sons**, which earns the highest marks at 90/100 for its emotionally devastating approach to Arthur Miller's classic. The production's minimalist aesthetic allows the ensemble cast to deliver performances of raw intensity that critics find both contemporary and timeless.

Close behind, **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** returns for its 20th anniversary with renewed relevance, reminding audiences why the show's blend of humor and heart resonated so deeply two decades ago. Meanwhile, **Paddington The Musical** has emerged as an unexpected critical darling, with reviewers marveling at the technical achievement of bringing the beloved bear to life on stage through innovative puppetry.

The season also showcases important new voices and revivals with renewed urgency. Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** explores language and identity with intelligence and nuance, while the revival of **Ragtime** finds fresh resonance in today's social climate, anchored by Joshua Henry's acclaimed performance. Branden Jacobs-Jenkins adds to his reputation with **Purpose**, another incisive examination of family dynamics, and Bess Wohl's **Liberation** tackles feminist themes through an ambitious structural approach.

For theatergoers seeking substance alongside spectacle this spring, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience Broadway's dramatic offerings before they close.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
